articles.title: FTC Moves to Hold 'Pharma Bro' Shkreli in Contempt — Caught Trading 60+ Drug Stocks Despite Lifetime Ban
articles.summary: Martin Shkreli, already convicted of securities fraud, allegedly violated a court-ordered lifetime ban from the pharmaceutical industry by trading stocks in at least 60 drug companies. The FTC and seven states are now seeking contempt findings and demanding he forfeit all trading profits. This is what happens when the pharma ecosystem's worst actors face no real deterrence — they simply keep playing.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Hid Device Safety Data From Investors — Stock Collapses 37% When Truth Emerges
articles.summary: Beta Bionics allegedly misled investors about the safety, efficacy, and commercial viability of its iLet medical device, triggering a securities fraud class action after shares cratered over 37%. If the company concealed safety signals from investors, the question becomes: what were regulators doing, and were patients informed? Device safety suppression and financial fraud are two sides of the same coin.

articles.title: Forced Treatment vs. Patient Autonomy: The State's Growing Power to Medicate Against Your Will
articles.summary: A Reason investigation asks the question the psychiatric establishment refuses to answer honestly: does a mental illness diagnosis strip you of the right to refuse treatment? Forced medication is expanding quietly through court systems and institutional policies, with little public debate and almost no mainstream media scrutiny. This is the psychiatric-state apparatus in action — and dissenting clinicians are being silenced.

articles.title: Estrogen, Serotonin, and Endotoxin: The Metabolic Framework Big Pharma Doesn't Want Taught in Med School
articles.summary: Researcher Georgi Dinkov breaks down how estrogen dominance, histamine dysregulation, serotonin excess, and endotoxin load interact to drive chronic disease — a framework rooted in the suppressed work of biologist Ray Peat. These mechanisms are routinely ignored in clinical training because they implicate dietary choices, endocrine disruptors, and gut dysfunction rather than patentable drugs. The implications for women's health, fertility, and metabolic disease are enormous.

articles.title: Ensign Group Hid Patient Neglect, Faked Staffing Data, and Billed Fraudulently — Securities Lawsuit Unmasks the Cover-Up
articles.summary: Nursing home giant Ensign Group is accused of concealing systematic patient neglect, manipulating quality and staffing metrics submitted to regulators, and running an administrator-license rental scheme — all while investors were told the business was sound. This is healthcare fraud operating at industrial scale, enabled by regulators who accepted falsified data at face value. Patients paid with their health; executives paid themselves.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Faces Federal Fraud Complaint: FTC Says Company Deceived Patients and Investors Alike
articles.summary: The FTC has filed a sweeping complaint against Hims & Hers Health, accusing the telehealth company of deceptive practices — now triggering a securities class action lawsuit against executives. The case raises urgent questions about how direct-to-consumer drug platforms operate outside traditional safety oversight and what patients were actually told about the products they were prescribed. The FDA-approved telehealth model is being stress-tested in real time.

articles.title: Pancreatic Cancer Cells Continuously Rewire Their DNA to Evade Treatment — The Standard Oncology Model Is Failing Patients
articles.summary: A landmark analysis of nearly half a million cells from pancreatic cancer patients reveals that tumor cells continuously reshape their genetic architecture over time, systematically outmaneuvering chemotherapy and targeted therapies. This finding directly challenges the static tumor model that underpins most approved treatment protocols — and raises the question of why metabolic and integrative approaches targeting cancer's adaptive biology remain unfunded and marginalized. Patients are dying while oncology orthodoxy resists paradigm change.

articles.title: Live Vaccines Accidentally Given to 220 Immunocompromised IBD Patients — Zero Adverse Outcomes Challenge Official Dogma
articles.summary: A real-world study found that 220 IBD patients on immunosuppressive biologics who accidentally received live vaccines — including MMR and varicella — suffered zero cases of measles, mumps, or chickenpox as a result. Current guidelines strictly prohibit these vaccines in this population, yet the data suggest the actual risk may be far lower than regulatory bodies claim. This is exactly the kind of safety evidence that should trigger guideline review — but rarely does.

articles.title: Pharma Bro Shkreli Caught Trading 60+ Drug Stocks Despite Lifetime Ban — FTC Seeks Contempt
articles.summary: The FTC and seven states allege Martin Shkreli secretly traded stocks in at least 60 pharmaceutical companies in direct violation of a court-ordered lifetime ban from the drug industry. Federal authorities are now seeking contempt charges and demanding he forfeit all profits. This case exposes the revolving door of pharma impunity — even those explicitly banned from the industry find ways back in.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Misled Investors on iLet Device Safety — Stock Craters 37% as Fraud Suit Filed
articles.summary: Beta Bionics allegedly concealed known safety and efficacy problems with its iLet medical device from investors, triggering a 37% stock collapse and a federal securities fraud class action. The company's claimed FDA compliance status is now under direct legal scrutiny. This is a textbook case of a medical device company burying adverse data to protect market position.

articles.title: Ensign Group Hid Patient Neglect, Manipulated Quality Data, and Ran a License Rental Scheme — Now Facing Fraud Suit
articles.summary: Ensign Group, a major care facility operator, is accused of concealing systemic patient neglect, understaffing, manipulated quality and staffing metrics, improper billing, and an administrator-license rental scheme from investors. The stock dropped 8% when the concealment began unraveling. When healthcare operators cook their own safety data, patients pay with their lives.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Faces Federal Fraud Complaint — FTC Says Company Deceived Patients on Drug Safety
articles.summary: The FTC has filed a sweeping federal complaint against Hims & Hers Health alleging the company and its executives deceived consumers, triggering a securities fraud class action. The charges center on misrepresentations about the safety and efficacy of its pharmaceutical offerings. A direct-to-consumer pharma model built on opacity is now facing the accountability it spent years avoiding.

articles.title: Forced Psychiatric Treatment: Courts Are Stripping Mentally Ill Patients of the Right to Refuse Medication
articles.summary: A Reason investigation examines the growing legal and institutional pressure to forcibly medicate individuals diagnosed with mental illness, gutting informed consent rights under the guise of therapeutic benefit. The piece raises direct questions about state power over the body and whether a psychiatric diagnosis effectively voids a patient's autonomy. With psychiatric overdiagnosis rampant and medication harms underreported, this trend should alarm anyone paying attention.

articles.title: Live Vaccines Given to 220 Immunocompromised IBD Patients Caused Zero Infections — So Why Is the Guidance Still Blanket Prohibition?
articles.summary: A study of 220 IBD patients on immunosuppressive biologics who accidentally received live vaccines for measles, mumps, or chickenpox recorded zero subsequent infections from those diseases. Despite this real-world safety signal, medical guidelines continue to categorically prohibit live vaccines in this population. The data suggests current guidance may be needlessly leaving immunocompromised patients unprotected from preventable disease.

articles.title: Pancreatic Cancer Cells Continuously Rewire Their Genetics to Escape Treatment — Half a Million Cells Tell the Story Oncology Ignored
articles.summary: Analysis of nearly 500,000 cells from dozens of pancreatic tumor patients reveals that cancer cells are in perpetual genetic flux, actively reshaping themselves to evade every treatment thrown at them. This fundamentally challenges the static tumor model that drives most oncology drug development and clinical trial design. The finding raises urgent questions about why the field continues pouring billions into targeted therapies against a moving target.

articles.title: Placental GDF15 Deficiency Drives Fetal Growth Restriction — A Pregnancy Suppression Signal the System Has Barely Discussed
articles.summary: New research in PLOS Biology demonstrates that placenta-specific GDF15 is essential for fetal growth, with deficiency causing restriction through disruption of the fetal hepatic STAT3-IGF2 axis. Clinical studies have already linked low GDF15 levels to fetal growth restriction in humans, yet this mechanistic pathway has received virtually no mainstream clinical attention. At a time when miscarriage and fetal growth data are politically charged, this metabolic pregnancy research deserves far more scrutiny.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Hid iLet Device Safety Failures From Investors — FDA Compliance Collapse Triggers Fraud Lawsuit
articles.summary: Beta Bionics allegedly misled investors about the safety, efficacy, and commercial viability of its iLet medical device, triggering a 37% stock collapse and a securities fraud class action. The company's FDA compliance failures were concealed while executives made public assurances. This is the pattern: device makers obscure safety data until the market forces disclosure that regulators should have demanded first.

articles.title: FTC Finally Moves on Shkreli — But Where Is the Same Energy for Pfizer, Merck, and AbbVie?
articles.summary: The FTC and seven states are seeking contempt charges against Martin Shkreli for allegedly trading stocks in at least 60 drug companies despite a lifetime ban — a brazen violation that exposes how porous the industry's so-called accountability structures truly are. Shkreli is the convenient villain pharma uses to distract from systemic price-fixing and data manipulation by far larger players. The question regulators won't answer: why is this level of scrutiny reserved for one ex-con while Big Pharma's revolving door spins freely?

articles.title: Forced Psychiatric Treatment: The State Declares Mental Illness Voids Your Bodily Autonomy
articles.summary: A Reason analysis challenges the legal and ethical framework allowing governments to mandate psychiatric treatment over patient refusal, exposing how the mental health system weaponizes diagnosis to strip individuals of informed consent rights. When the state can override your 'no' with a DSM code, the psychiatric establishment becomes an instrument of coercion, not care. This is the rarely-reported collision between overdiagnosis, psychiatric overreach, and the erosion of medical self-determination.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Faces Federal Fraud Complaint — FTC Says Executives Deceived Patients and Investors Simultaneously
articles.summary: The FTC has filed a sweeping federal complaint against Hims & Hers Health, accusing company executives of deceiving both patients and investors — a dual fraud that exposes how telehealth platforms can exploit regulatory gaps to prioritize revenue over clinical honesty. A securities class action has now followed, with a November 2026 lead plaintiff deadline. When the business model is built on overpromising treatments, patients pay with their health and investors pay with their money.

An 8% stock drop followed the exposure of practices that regulators should have caught years earlier. This is what happens when CMS oversight is performative and nursing home chains operate in the dark.

articles.title: Pancreatic Cancer Cells Continuously Evolve to Escape Treatment — And the Oncology Establishment Is Just Now Noticing
articles.summary: A landmark analysis of nearly half a million cells from dozens of pancreatic tumor patients reveals that cancer cells continuously reprogram their genetic identity over time, systematically evading standard-of-care treatments. This dynamic plasticity model challenges the static tumor-genetics paradigm that has dominated oncology funding and drug development for decades. The implications for chemotherapy-first protocols are damning — and the silence from treatment guideline bodies is deafening.

articles.title: IBD Patients Got Live Vaccines While on Immunosuppressants — And Nothing Happened. So Why Is the Warning Still There?
articles.summary: A study of 220 IBD patients who accidentally received live vaccines for measles, mumps, or chickenpox while on immune-modifying biologics recorded zero cases of vaccine-strain disease — directly challenging the standing clinical prohibition that has denied these patients standard immunization for years. The guideline banning live vaccines in immunocompromised patients has never been robustly tested in prospective trials, yet it remains entrenched in practice. This accidental natural experiment demands a formal reassessment that vaccine orthodoxy has no incentive to conduct.

articles.title: GDF15 Deficiency Drives Fetal Growth Restriction — A Placental Mechanism Medicine Has Overlooked for Decades
articles.summary: New research published in PLOS Biology identifies placenta-specific GDF15 as a critical regulator of fetal growth through the hepatic STAT3-IGF2 signaling axis — a mechanism entirely absent from mainstream obstetric screening and antenatal care protocols. Clinical data has long correlated low circulating GDF15 with fetal growth restriction, yet this pathway has received almost no translational research funding. Women experiencing unexplained fetal growth restriction may have been failed by a field that never looked at the placenta's own signaling chemistry.

articles.title: Forced Psychiatric Treatment: The Government's New Weapon Against Medical Autonomy
articles.summary: A Reason analysis tears into the legal and ethical framework being used to strip mentally ill patients of their right to refuse medication — a right that healthy citizens take for granted. Forced treatment regimes benefit institutional psychiatry and pharmaceutical manufacturers who profit from captive patient populations. This is coercion dressed up as care, and it deserves to be named as such.

articles.title: Estrogen, Serotonin, and Endotoxin: The Metabolic Framework Mainstream Medicine Refuses to Teach
articles.summary: Georgi Dinkov lays out the interconnected hormonal and metabolic mechanisms — estrogen dominance, histamine excess, serotonin toxicity, and endotoxin load — that conventional medicine either ignores or actively suppresses in favor of pharmaceutical intervention. Patients are routinely told their labs are 'normal' while their symptoms scream otherwise, because the metabolic model threatens the entire drug-prescribing paradigm. This is the alternative disease framework Big Pharma cannot monetize and therefore will not fund.

articles.title: Pharma Bro Shkreli Caught Trading 60+ Drug Stocks Under a Lifetime Ban — The System Only Enforces Rules It Chooses
articles.summary: The FTC and seven states allege Martin Shkreli violated his lifetime ban on pharmaceutical industry participation by secretly trading stocks in at least 60 drug companies. While this case involves a convicted fraudster, it exposes how thoroughly industry insiders believe pharma rules are optional — and how long regulators look the other way. The same regulatory capture that let Shkreli operate unchecked for years is the culture rotting the FDA and NIH from within.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Hid Safety Problems With Its iLet Device — Investors and Patients Both Got Burned
articles.summary: A securities fraud class action reveals that Beta Bionics allegedly misled investors about the safety, efficacy, and commercial performance of its iLet medical device, triggering a 37% stock collapse when the truth emerged. If the company lied to Wall Street about safety, patients using the device deserve to know what was concealed and when. The FDA's failure to catch or publicize these issues before the market had to do it for them is its own indictment.

articles.title: Ensign Group Buried Patient Neglect, Falsified Quality Data, and Billed for Care That Never Happened
articles.summary: A securities fraud lawsuit against Ensign Group alleges the company concealed systematic patient neglect, manipulated staffing and quality metrics reported to regulators, ran an illegal administrator-license rental scheme, and submitted improper billing to federal health programs. This is not a compliance footnote — it is a blueprint for how for-profit healthcare operators exploit elderly patients while gaming CMS oversight. Regulators had the data and apparently looked away.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Faces Federal Fraud Complaint — Telehealth's Darling Built on Deception, FTC Says
articles.summary: The FTC has filed a sweeping federal complaint against Hims & Hers Health, and a securities class action has followed, alleging executives misled investors while the company allegedly engaged in deceptive practices with consumers. The telehealth sector has been celebrated as disruptive and patient-centered, but this case suggests the disruption included deceiving the very patients it claimed to liberate from traditional medicine. The question regulators refuse to ask: who was protecting patients while this was happening?
